name: Mitochondrion
short_description: The power plant: a smooth outer membrane and a deeply folded inner one whose folds (cristae) multiply the working surface. There sits the respiratory chain, which turns nutrients and oxygen into ATP, the cell's energy currency.

textbook.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image, accepted on the first attempt; a clean cutaway of a single elongated bean-shaped mitochondrion. A single smooth, unbroken steel-blue outer membrane wraps a thin pale intermembrane space and a separate brick-red inner membrane; that inner membrane is thrown into many deep transverse folds - the cristae - every one of them clearly attached to the boundary membrane at both ends, never a detached free-floating shelf, and all projecting into a fully enclosed cream-tan matrix running the length of the organelle. In the matrix sits one small tangled golden ring of mitochondrial DNA - unmistakably circular - a scatter of slate-grey mitoribosome granules, and small green mushroom-shaped ATP synthase knobs studding the matrix-facing tips of several cristae. Muted educational palette, thin clean outlines, dark charcoal ground, edge-to-edge fill, no text, no border. Exactly one specimen)

sem.1: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the science is correct - single specimen, smooth outer membrane, cristae connected to the inner membrane and radiating into a fully enclosed matrix with a circular gold mtDNA loop, mitoribosome dots and green ATP-synthase knobs - but the rendering style is a flat, clean vector/cartoon illustration rather than a photorealistic false-colour SEM plate: no photographic surface grain, no crisp specular fracture texture. Style-consistency fail per the SEM rubric (must look like a real false-colour micrograph). Fix-prompt: same science, explicitly demand photographic grain, fracture-edge specular highlights and real material roughness, forbid a flat vector/cartoon look)
sem.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; a genuine improvement in photorealism - fine grainy surface noise, crisp specular highlights along the freeze-fracture edges, real textured roughness on the outer membrane, the cristae and the granular matrix, with a softly blurred textured background giving true depth of field. Cristae remain clearly continuous with the inner membrane at their base, projecting into a fully enclosed, granular matrix holding a circular gold mtDNA loop, slate mitoribosome dots and green ATP-synthase knobs at the crista tips. Single specimen, false-colour palette, cool studio lighting, edge-to-edge, no text, no border)

3d.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; every individual structure is correct in isolation - double membrane, connected cristae, enclosed matrix, circular gold mtDNA, mitoribosome dots, green ATP-synthase knobs, natural biological tints - but the composition is wrong: the organelle reads as TWO separate mirrored C-shaped halves with a visible gap/waist between them, essentially a bisected or duplicated specimen rather than one single continuous mitochondrion. Fails the 'exactly one specimen, one continuous outer boundary' rule. Fix-prompt: demand ONE single continuous, unbroken outer silhouette with no waist, pinch, gap or mirror-symmetry split, one continuous central matrix channel)
3d.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; now a single, continuous, unbroken capsule-shaped organelle - the outer steel-blue membrane forms one unbroken boundary around a gently waisted but fully continuous body. The brick-red inner membrane is thrown into many deep folds forming a dense lattice attached to the boundary on the outside and bordering one single continuous cream matrix channel running the full length down the centre; the matrix holds a circular gold mtDNA ring, slate mitoribosome dots and small green ATP-synthase knobs at several crista tips. Natural believable biological tones (steel-blue, brick-red, cream, gold, slate, soft green) - not monochrome, not neon. Soft global illumination, clean dark studio ground, edge-to-edge, single specimen, no text, no border. Minor honest note: the cristae read as a fine woven lattice/mesh rather than individually distinct comb-like fins, a legibility simplification rather than a science error - every part of the mesh still stays attached to the boundary and borders the enclosed matrix, so the connected-cristae / enclosed-matrix relationship is intact)

watercolor.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image, accepted on the first attempt; warm aged paper fills the entire frame edge-to-edge and corner-to-corner with a soft darker wash halo directly on the paper - no mat, no border, no frame, no sheet-on-a-surface. A single tall bean/figure-eight shaped mitochondrion painted large and centred: fine ink outlines trace a smooth unfolded outer membrane in steel-blue wash, a separate brick-red inner membrane thrown into deep hairpin-loop folds - the cristae - each one clearly a continuous loop of the inner membrane rather than a free island, projecting into a fully enclosed pale cream-tan matrix. A small tangled golden-yellow ring (mtDNA) sits in the lower matrix with slate-grey mitoribosome dots nearby, and small soft-green dots (ATP synthase) mark the inner tips of several cristae loops. Fine ink linework over translucent washes, no text, no arrows, no scale bar, single specimen)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons "Mitochondria - TEM.jpg", Public domain, Louisa Howard, Rippel Electron Microscope Facility, Dartmouth College, JEOL 100CX TEM, thin section of mammalian lung tissue. Viewed directly: a single, isolated, elongated mitochondrion fills most of the frame. Along its upper edge the outer membrane and inner membrane both appear as a tight double line with the intermembrane space between them. More than ten sharp, dark, transverse cristae cross the organelle, every one of them clearly continuous with the inner membrane - no detached shelves - projecting into a uniformly dense, fully enclosed granular matrix. Cleaned with NO image-editing model: a deterministic local crop removed the plain white caption/scale-bar footer bar confined to the bottom ~25 px of the 640x480 original, then a centred square crop (455x455) and a Lanczos resize to 1080x1080 (a 2.37x upscale, recorded explicitly in the sidecar) produced the final text-free reference. Nothing was invented, re-illustrated or reframed - the structure is exactly as photographed, only cropped and resized)
decision: use as final and as the primary labelled figure; double membrane, cristae connected to the inner membrane at both ends, fully enclosed matrix, circular gold mtDNA loop and correctly placed ATP-synthase knobs all landed correctly on gemini-2.5-flash-image's first attempt

use as final; attempt 1 was scientifically correct but stylistically a flat vector/cartoon illustration rather than a photorealistic false-colour SEM plate, which is a style-consistency fail per the SEM rubric; attempt 2 explicitly demanded photographic grain and fracture-edge texture and delivered a convincing false-colour freeze-fracture look while keeping every structural detail correct. Not labelled (SEM is the surface/cutaway comparison plate, following the same convention as the other organelles in this set)

use as final; labelled figure built. Attempt 1 was rejected outright for composition, not science - the organelle read as two separate mirrored halves with a gap between them rather than one continuous specimen; attempt 2 fixed this with an explicit single-continuous-boundary instruction and kept all the correct structural science. Honest caveat: the cristae render as a fine woven lattice rather than individually distinct comb-like folds - a legibility simplification, not a scientific error, since every part of the lattice still attaches to the boundary membrane and borders the one enclosed matrix channel

use as final and labelled with black-on-paper ink; full-bleed aged paper, correct double membrane, cristae drawn as connected hairpin loops (not detached islands) around a fully enclosed matrix holding a circular gold mtDNA ring, on the first attempt
